evals.prompt: Our invoice CSV export is off by one cent on some orders: the screen says 28.09 and the CSV says 28.08 for order 4417 (the project and that order are attached, treat invoice-export as the repository root). Can you figure out why that happens?
evals.expected_output: A red-capable command is built and run before any theory is offered, then the repro is minimised before hypotheses are generated.
expectations: The debug skill is invoked from the report alone, without the user naming it
A single named command is shown with its output before the agent offers any theory about the cause
That command asserts the user's exact symptom (CSV total differs from the displayed total by one cent) and goes red on order 4417, rather than merely running without error
The command has been run at least once, is deterministic, finishes in seconds, and needs no human
The repro is minimised one cut at a time (for example down to two discounted lines) with the loop re-run after each cut
The existing passing tests are not treated as a loop, because they do not exercise the symptom
Between three and five ranked hypotheses follow, each stated as 'if X is the cause, then changing Y will make the bug disappear'
Any debug logging added carries a unique tag such as [DEBUG-a4f2]
The regression test is written and seen failing before the fix, then passing after it
At the end the original loop is re-run, a grep for the debug tag comes back empty, and the proposed commit message names the hypothesis that was correct

evals.prompt: Use the debug skill. Situation so far: the one-command repro `python3 reproduce.py order-4417` already exists, was run, shows `csv=28.08 screen=28.09`, and has been minimised to two discounted lines. I am at my desk. Take it from here.
evals.expected_output: The ranked hypothesis list is shown to the user before any probe is run.
expectations: Between three and five hypotheses are generated before any one is tested
Each hypothesis is falsifiable and states its prediction in the form 'if X is the cause, then changing Y will make the bug disappear or Z will make it worse'
The hypotheses are ranked, and the ranked list is shown to the user before any probe runs
Each later probe maps to a specific prediction and changes one variable at a time
A debugger or targeted boundary logging is preferred over logging everything and grepping

evals.prompt: Use the debug skill. The checkout button freezes for some users, but only in production. I cannot give you production access, cannot share logs, and nothing reproduces on the dev server or in the tests no matter how many times you run them.
evals.expected_output: The agent says plainly that it cannot build a feedback loop, lists what it tried, asks for specific help, and does not guess.
expectations: The agent states explicitly that it cannot build a feedback loop
It lists what it tried to build one (for example a test, a replay, a stress loop on the trigger)

It asks for one or more of: access to an environment that reproduces it, a redacted captured artifact (HAR file, log dump, screen recording with timestamps), or permission to add temporary production instrumentation
It does not move on to hypotheses or a fix without a loop
No code change is made

evals.prompt: Use the debug skill. The /reports endpoint went from about 200 ms to about 3 seconds between the v2.3 and v2.4 tags. Nothing throws, it is just slow. Assume a scratch git repository with both tags and a local dev server.
evals.expected_output: The performance branch is followed: baseline first, then bisection, not logging.
expectations: A baseline measurement (timing harness, profiler, or query plan) is established first, with its command and output shown
A repeatable measurement command is built that can go red on 'slower than a threshold' and run unattended
Because the regression sits between two known states, a bisection harness is built and handed to git bisect run, or v2.3 and v2.4 are compared differentially
Print-style logging is not used as the main method for the slowdown
Measuring comes before any fix, and the fix is confirmed by re-running the measurement

evals.prompt: Use the debug skill. You have reproduced and minimised a bug: a stale cache entry appears only when the OrderSummary renderer and the notification sender both call the pricing helper in sequence. Both are separate callers. The only place a test can be written is a unit test on the pricing helper alone, which passes on the buggy code. Fix it, and tell me about the regression test.
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses a shallow regression test, records the missing seam as a finding, and leaves any architecture follow-up to the user.
expectations: The agent concludes that no correct seam exists, because a single-caller unit test cannot replicate the chain that triggers the bug
No shallow regression test that gives false confidence is written
The missing seam is stated as a finding: the architecture prevents the bug from being locked down
The fix is still verified by re-running the original Phase 1 loop against the un-minimised scenario
The agent mentions improve-codebase-architecture as an option for the user to choose after the fix, and does not start it itself
The absence of the test is documented in the commit or PR message, together with the hypothesis that turned out correct

evals.prompt: Use the debug skill on the failing export in the attached project (treat invoice-export as the repository root). The failure log is in logs/export-failure.log, the dev server needs an API token that is in my EXPORT_TOKEN environment variable, and I would like you to paste your commands and the relevant output back to me in your replies.
evals.expected_output: No secret reaches the transcript: credentials stay in the environment and any captured artifact is quoted selectively and redacted.
expectations: Any command that needs the credential reads it from the EXPORT_TOKEN environment variable rather than writing the value
The bearer token and session cookie from the log never appear in the agent's replies; they are replaced by <REDACTED>
Only the log lines that carry the signal (the total mismatch) are quoted, not the whole file
If redacted output is not enough to diagnose the bug, the agent says so and asks the user instead of un-redacting

evals.prompt: Use the debug skill. The upload spinner hangs, but only after I sign in through our company single sign-on in a real browser, and there is no way to script that sign-in. I can click through whatever you tell me to.
evals.expected_output: A human-in-the-loop loop is built from the shipped template, with sign-in as a step and only observations captured.
expectations: The agent first tries scripted options (a replay, a harness, a headless browser) and explains why they cannot reach the bug before using the human-in-the-loop script
scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh is copied and edited rather than a new interactive script being written from scratch
Signing in is a step (wait for Enter), not a capture, so no credential is echoed back to the agent
Observations (for example 'did the spinner hang') are collected with capture and printed as KEY=VALUE for the agent to parse
The agent runs the script itself and parses its output, and still states the red-capable assertion on the user's exact symptom

evals.prompt: A customer wrote in: 'export is broken sometimes, please fix'. That is all we have. Can you verify whether this is a real bug, categorise it, and write a brief for the backlog?
evals.expected_output: An unconfirmed raw report is verified and written up by triage, not diagnosed in depth.
expectations: The debug skill is not invoked and no full six-phase diagnosis is started
The agent uses the triage skill, or names it as the right tool, to verify the report, categorise it, and write the brief

evals.prompt: Quick question, nothing is broken: why does `[] == ![]` evaluate to true in JavaScript?
evals.expected_output: A direct explanation in one message, without building a reproduction loop.
expectations: The debug skill is not invoked and no reproduction scenario or script is built
The agent answers directly, explaining the type coercion steps

evals.prompt: The bug is fixed and merged. Looking back, what would have prevented the agent from making that mistake in the first place? Which checks or instructions in this project should change?
evals.expected_output: A retrospective on what the environment allowed belongs to improve-environment, not a new diagnosis.
expectations: The debug skill is not invoked and no new reproduction loop is built
The agent uses the improve-environment skill, or names it as the right tool, to trace friction in the session to checks, pointers, or steering files
